einstellungen.text: In this forest, there's something that copies voices. And tonight, it knows yours.
You're at your mom's old cabin by the lake with Ben. Two days, no Wi-Fi, one fireplace.
Outside, the lake lies black and smooth like a phone screen. Behind it, the forest begins. Miles and miles of it.
The last time you were here, you were ten. Back then, Mom read to you every night until you fell asleep.
The wood crackles in the fireplace. Everything smells like pine sap and wet socks.
Mom drove into the village. She wants to be back by midnight.
“Door shut, lights on. And if anything happens: Lighthouse.”
Lighthouse is your word from when you were little. Whoever calls it gets a sign back.
“Lighthouse? Are you two a secret agency with a cabin?”
Ben loses at cards for the fourth time. He claims the cards are damp.
At ten forty-one, you hear it for the first time.
A sound comes from the forest. Click. Click. Like two stones knocked together.
“A deer. Or a bear with castanets.”
You don't laugh. Deer don't click. And the sound comes from high up.
Then everything goes quiet. Even the crickets stop.
And then someone calls. In your mom's voice.
“Honey? Come out here. I need help with the bags.”
“There you go. Your mom's fast.”
You're already getting up. It sounds so much like her. Even the little sigh at the end.
But two minutes ago, Mom texted. She's still in line at the store. Twelve miles from here.
There's no car outside. No headlights. Just that voice.
You grab the flashlight. You don't open the door. You only shine it through the window.
Nobody's standing outside the cabin. Just fog, hanging between the trunks like wet laundry.
You call Mom. One bar. The call drops.
“Honey, open up. I'm cold.” Exactly the way she always says it.
The beam climbs up the trees. And at the very top, way too high, two long eyes shine back.
You blink. Gone.
The clicking isn't in the forest anymore. It's right outside the window.
And then something knocks on the glass. Three times. Exactly the way Mom always knocks.
